title: ADWIN Algorithm: Covariate Drift Detection and Response
content:
## ADWIN Overview
ADaptive WINdowing (ADWIN) is an online drift detection algorithm that maintains an adaptive sliding window over a data stream. It detects drift by comparing statistics across sub-windows and triggers an alarm when the difference exceeds a significance threshold.

## Score Interpretation
- ADWIN score 0.0–0.10: No drift detected. Window is stable.
- ADWIN score 0.10–0.20: Early drift signal. Monitor closely. Do not act immediately.
- ADWIN score 0.20–0.30: Confirmed covariate drift. Schedule investigation.
- ADWIN score > 0.30: Severe drift. Immediate investigation required. Retrain likely.

## Distinguishing Covariate vs Concept Drift
- **Covariate drift**: Input distribution P(X) changes. Model may still generalize if decision boundary unchanged.
- **Concept drift**: Joint distribution P(Y|X) changes. Model accuracy will degrade. Retrain required.

## ADWIN Diagnostic Protocol
1. Identify the feature(s) triggering ADWIN alarm.
2. Check prediction accuracy metrics (AUC, F1) — did they drop alongside ADWIN?
3. If accuracy is stable: likely covariate drift only. Monitor.
4. If accuracy dropped: likely concept drift. Prepare retrain.

## Correlation Analysis
- Correlate ADWIN alarm timestamp with:
  - Model version deploy time
  - Data ingestion pipeline changes
  - Upstream service API changes
  - Business events (new product launch, market change)

## Response Matrix
| ADWIN Score | Accuracy Impact | Action |
|-------------|-----------------|--------|
| 0.15–0.20   | None            | Monitor |
| 0.20–0.30   | Minor (<2%)     | Prepare retrain |
| 0.20–0.30   | Major (>5%)     | Emergency retrain |
| >0.30       | Any             | Rollback + retrain |
